sections.title: Marking a wanted event as not-yet-real
sections.content: Verbs of wanting and requesting — akar ("to want"), szeretné (definite "would like"), kér ("to ask for") — take a hogy-clause whose verb is in the -jon/-jen form, not the plain present tense. Azt akarom, hogy sikerüljön literally says "I want that it succeed" — English drops this into a plain infinitive ("I want it to succeed"), but Hungarian marks the wanted event as not-yet-real with -jon/-jen, the same form you just learned.

sections.title: Wanting something to happen
rows: Azt akarom, hogy sikerüljön a tervem.
I want my plan to succeed.
Azt szeretném, hogy fejlődjön a karrierem.
I would like my career to develop/progress.
I ask that you be patient. (formal)

items.spanish: Azt szeretném, hogy megvalósuljon az álmom.
items.english: I would like my dream to come true.

items.spanish: Azt akarom, hogy minden lépés közelebb vigyen a célomhoz.
items.english: I want every step to bring me closer to my goal.

sections.content: Azt is doing quiet work here — it's a placeholder pointing forward to the hogy-clause, the same "pointing" job you saw az lenne a megoldás do in A2. Drop azt and Akarom, hogy sikerüljön still works, but Azt akarom, hogy... is the more natural, more common shape.
